Doc.Summary: Raised when a tracked flyout closed, however it was closed.
The opacity of the shapes outside the entered group, 0 to 1. It comes from the theme.
The shape that is being drawn, in screen space. It is not part of the document.
The entered group. Shapes outside it are drawn faded (see PressToShape.App.Workspace.CanvasScene). null when no group is entered.
The brush of the grid lines. It comes from the theme.
The distance between grid lines in document units.
The brush of the snap guide lines. It comes from the theme.
The side of a selection handle in screen pixels. It comes from the theme, so a layout for touch can draw larger handles.
A shape that is not drawn because the draft takes its place (a path that is being continued). null hides nothing.
The nodes and handles of the selected shapes for Direct Select and the Node tool, in screen space. They are drawn over the shapes.
Position of the artboard's left edge in this control, in screen pixels.
Position of the artboard's top edge in this control, in screen pixels.
What is drawn for the selection, in screen space: outlines, frame, handles and the box being dragged.
The nodes and handles of the path that the Pen is drawing, in screen space. They are drawn over the shapes.
The brush of a ruler guide that the drag is snapped to. It comes from the theme.
The brush of a ruler guide. It comes from the theme.
The brush of the selected ruler guide. It comes from the theme.
The ruler guides in screen space. They are drawn as lines across the whole control, over the shapes.
The brush of the selection outlines, handle outlines and the selection box. It comes from the theme.
The fill of the handles. It comes from the theme.
Whether the grid is drawn, behind the shapes.
The brush of the lines of the smart guide markers. It comes from the theme.
The background of the numbers of the smart guide markers. It comes from the theme.
The brush of the numbers of the smart guide markers. It comes from the theme.
The markers and labels of the smart guides in screen space. They are drawn last.
The guide lines of the object a drag is snapped to, in screen space. They are drawn over everything else.
Lays out the texts of the document. Without one, texts are not drawn.
Zoom in percent. 100 means one document unit per screen pixel.
Position of document zero along the ruler, in screen pixels.
Zoom in percent. 100 means one document pixel per screen pixel.
Ends the editing. Run on Escape and when the editor loses the focus to another control.
The content of the text. The user's typing is written back to it.
The brush of the text when the text has no fill. It comes from the theme.
The height of a line in screen pixels. NaN leaves it to the font.
The text that is edited, in screen space with its font. null when nothing is edited: the control is then empty.

Doc.Summary: One tick of the timer. Public to the tests only.
Puts the touch sizes into the resources of root. Does nothing if the application has no such dictionary.
The radius of the center disc. Wedges start here.
The outer radius of the wedges.
The box that is typed in. For tests.
The time source. Tests replace it so they need no real time.
Run when the button was held down long enough.
A titled section whose whole header row toggles the content. Used by the inspector panels. The look is defined in Styles/Controls.axaml.

Draws the shapes of a document. It only draws: PressToShape.App.Workspace.CanvasScene decides what is drawn and where. Shape colors are document data, so this control uses no theme brushes. It does not handle pointer input.
How far a glyph run moves the pen. It is the sum of the glyph advances, not the width of the ink (Avalonia.Media.GlyphRun.Bounds).

What a number text box does with focus and keys, for every view that shows PressToShape.App.ViewModels.Editor.NumberFieldViewModels: the value is applied when the box is left or Enter is pressed, and the shown value comes back on Escape. A text box takes part when its Tag holds its field view model. The handlers sit on the view, so keys in other text boxes keep their meaning. The view model decides what the value means.

Knows which of some flyouts are open, so the Back button can close the last one that was opened before anything else happens. A menu is not part of a view model, so this is a view-only helper. Used by the tablet toolbar (overflow menu) and the tablet status bar (zoom list).

The ring context menu. It fills the canvas area (so a press beside the ring is caught here and closes it), and draws the wedges, their icons and the center around the point where the ring was opened. It draws what PressToShape.App.ViewModels.Editor.RingMenuViewModel holds and forwards pointer and key input to it; PressToShape.App.Workspace.RingGeometry does the math. The colors and sizes come from the theme (see the styles of the classes ringWedge, ringIcon, ringCenter and ringCenterText).

A horizontal or vertical ruler. It asks PressToShape.App.Workspace.RulerTicks for the ticks of the current zoom and origin and draws them with the theme brushes. It does not know about documents or the canvas.

The editor of a text on the canvas: a borderless Avalonia.Controls.TextBox at the place of the text, with its font and its rotation, so the user types where the text is. It brings the caret, the selection, the clipboard, the input method and the on-screen keyboard. The control only shows what the view model gives it and reports the content and the end of the editing: it decides nothing about the document.

The button of a tool group in the tablet tool column. A tap selects the current tool of the group (see PressToShape.App.Controls.ToolToggleButton). Holding the pointer down for a while runs PressToShape.App.Controls.ToolGroupButton.LongPressCommand (which opens the flyout of the group), and the click that follows the release is then swallowed, so a long press never also selects the tool. The decision is made by PressToShape.App.Workspace.LongPressTracker; this control only passes it pointer events and the time. It looks like a plain toggle button, so the tool styles apply to it.

A toggle button for something whose state lives in a view model: a tool in the tool column, or the icon that shows whether a panel is open. Its checked state comes only from the binding. A tap runs the command and does not flip the button by itself, so tapping the active tool again keeps it active (a plain toggle button would show it as off while the tool is still the active one, and would also lose its binding). It looks like a plain toggle button, so the tool styles apply.

The sizes for touch and stylus, defined in Styles/Theme.axaml as the dictionary TouchSizes. The tablet layout applies them to its root, so every control below it that looks a size up with DynamicResource gets the touch value, and the desktop keeps its own. The dictionary cannot simply be merged, because Avalonia allows a dictionary only one owner. Its entries are copied instead.
